profiles.remarkableResult: Led sound experiences at the MET, Lincoln Center, and MoMA PS1. Featured in The New York Times, Vogue, and TIME. Her book 'Sound Bath' was published by a major publisher (Tiller Press/Simon & Schuster). She became the go-to sound healer for Fortune 500 companies and luxury brands, bringing sound healing into mainstream corporate wellness.

profiles.name: Sharon Salzberg
profiles.bio: One of the three founders of Insight Meditation Society who brought Vipassana from Burma to middle America, making loving-kindness meditation a household practice
profiles.oneLiner: You are worthy of love simply because you exist
profiles.blowUpMoment: "Real Happiness" hit NYT bestseller list 2011, ~40 years after she started teaching
profiles.blowUpContext: She had been a leading meditation teacher for 35+ years, co-founding IMS in 1975 and writing several books, but her mainstream visibility grew with the mindfulness movement.

create.evidence: Primary Western popularizer of Metta (lovingkindness) as standalone practice

capture.evidence: NYT bestselling author, 50+ years teaching

portable.evidence: IMS and Barre Center train teachers. Metta taught by thousands worldwide.

profiles.ruleBreak: Rejected the idea that loving-kindness (metta) meditation was a soft, secondary practice. In Western Buddhist circles, insight meditation (vipassana) was the 'serious' practice and metta was considered supplementary or even sentimental. Salzberg made loving-kindness the main event, arguing it was as rigorous and transformative as any concentration practice.
profiles.twoWorlds: Lost both parents by childhood (father left at 4, mother died at 9, father returned at 11 then was institutionalized). Her personal suffering drove her to India at 18 where she found metta practice. Combined deep personal loss with classical Theravada Buddhist meditation.
profiles.stupidSimplicity: The most radical thing you can do is offer yourself kindness.
profiles.remarkableResult: Co-founded the Insight Meditation Society (IMS) in 1976, which became the most influential meditation center in North America. Her book 'Lovingkindness' (1995) has been continuously in print for 30+ years and is considered the definitive Western text on metta. She's been teaching meditation for over 50 years and her work helped mainstream mindfulness across American culture.

profiles.name: Shiva Rea
profiles.bio: A UCLA-trained yoga scholar who created Prana Vinyasa Flow, blending ecstatic movement, world music, and yoga into a devotional dance-like practice
profiles.oneLiner: Move with the pulse of life
profiles.blowUpMoment: Gaiam DVDs early 2000s, Vanity Fair "Madonna of yoga" 2007
profiles.blowUpContext: She was teaching yoga at UCLA and developing her Prana Vinyasa method, known for her fusion of movement, music, and yoga philosophy.

create.evidence: Created Prana Vinyasa. Trademarked system. 50+ Namaskars.

capture.evidence: DVDs, Yoga Journal, festival headliner

portable.evidence: 20+ year teacher training (200/300/500 hour)

profiles.ruleBreak: Rejected the rigid, pose-by-pose sequencing of traditional yoga. While most yoga was taught as a series of static postures held and released, Shiva Rea introduced 'Prana Vinyasa' — continuous, wave-like, rhythmic flow where movement never fully stops, modeled on ocean currents and natural cycles rather than linear sequences.
profiles.twoWorlds: Dance and movement arts meets classical yoga philosophy and Ayurveda. She brought the fluidity, musicality, and creative expression of dance into a practice rooted in ancient Tantric yoga philosophy and seasonal Ayurvedic cycles.
profiles.stupidSimplicity: Your body is a wave — stop treating it like a machine.
profiles.remarkableResult: Featured on over 15 yoga DVD bestsellers, named one of Yoga Journal's most influential yoga teachers, created the Global Mala Project (worldwide yoga events for charity), and leads large-scale yoga festivals and trainings across 6 continents.

profiles.name: Stan Tatkin
profiles.early_revenue_description: Ran a private couples therapy practice in LA while developing PACT.
profiles.ruleBreak: Rejected the individual-focused therapy model AND the idea that attachment styles are fixed traits. While the therapy world was telling people 'you're anxious-attached, here's how to cope,' Tatkin said attachment is co-created in real-time between two nervous systems. He shifted the focus from individual attachment labels to the 'couple bubble' — the two-person system you build together.
profiles.twoWorlds: Neuroscience (specifically psychobiology and polyvagal theory) meets couples therapy. He studied under Allan Schore and brought hard neuroscience — arousal regulation, facial recognition, threat detection — into the couples therapy room in a way that therapists and couples could actually apply.
profiles.stupidSimplicity: Secure your couple bubble first — two nervous systems protecting each other solve everything else.
profiles.remarkableResult: PACT (Psychobiological Approach to Couple Therapy) has trained thousands of therapists internationally. His book 'Wired for Love' became a relationship classic. He created one of the few couples therapy approaches that explicitly integrates neuroscience. PACT is now a recognized modality with a formal training institute. He remains actively influential in the couples therapy world.

profiles.name: Stanislav Grof
profiles.bio: A Czech psychiatrist who mapped the psyche's deepest layers through 4,500+ LSD sessions before inventing Holotropic Breathwork when the drug became illegal
profiles.oneLiner: The psyche has its own inner healing intelligence
profiles.blowUpMoment: Co-developed Holotropic Breathwork at Esalen (1973-1987), launched GTT certification 1989
profiles.blowUpContext: He was a clinical psychiatrist at the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center running government-approved LSD therapy research for over a decade.

create.evidence: Invented Holotropic Breathwork as non-pharmacological alternative to psychedelic therapy

capture.evidence: 20+ books, academic lectures, but no mainstream media pursuit

portable.evidence: GTT certification training 35+ years, facilitators worldwide

profiles.ruleBreak: Rejected the premise that therapeutic healing requires years of talk therapy and rational analysis. While mainstream psychiatry insisted on cognitive, verbal processing, Grof proved that non-ordinary states of consciousness (first via LSD, then via breathwork) could access and resolve deep trauma in hours rather than years.
profiles.twoWorlds: Clinical psychiatry and psychedelic research meets cartography of the psyche and transpersonal psychology. He was a rigorously trained Czech psychiatrist who became perhaps the world's foremost researcher on LSD-assisted psychotherapy, then created an entirely new map of the human unconscious.
profiles.stupidSimplicity: The psyche already knows how to heal itself — you just have to get out of its way.
profiles.remarkableResult: Conducted 4,500+ LSD-assisted psychotherapy sessions across Prague and Maryland. Co-developed Holotropic Breathwork with Christina Grof as a non-drug alternative. Helped establish transpersonal psychology as a field.

profiles.name: Sue Johnson
profiles.early_revenue_description: Held a clinical psychology faculty position at the University of Ottawa.
profiles.ruleBreak: Rejected the behavioral/cognitive approach to couples therapy that dominated the field (fixing communication patterns, teaching 'I statements'). Proved that relationship distress is fundamentally about attachment panic — when you fight about dishes, you're actually asking 'Are you there for me?' Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) made emotions the treatment, not the problem.
profiles.twoWorlds: Attachment theory (John Bowlby's work on infant-caregiver bonds) meets adult romantic relationships. She took a theory everyone assumed only applied to children and proved it explains adult love with the same precision — adults need a secure base just like infants do.
profiles.stupidSimplicity: Every fight is really just one question: 'Are you there for me?'
profiles.remarkableResult: EFT is now the most empirically validated couples therapy approach in existence — over 35 years of peer-reviewed research showing 70-75% recovery rates for distressed couples, with results holding at follow-up. Her book 'Hold Me Tight' sold over a million copies. EFT is practiced in over 40 countries. She essentially won the 'what works in couples therapy' debate.

profiles.name: Tara Brach
profiles.bio: A clinical psychologist and Buddhist meditation teacher whose weekly podcast became the gateway drug to mindfulness for millions of stressed professionals
profiles.oneLiner: Radical acceptance transforms everything it touches
profiles.blowUpMoment: Podcast (2010) quietly grew to 3M+ monthly downloads
profiles.blowUpContext: She was a clinical psychologist and founding teacher of the Insight Meditation Community of Washington DC, teaching meditation and leading retreats for decades.

create.evidence: Developed RAIN method (Recognize, Allow, Investigate, Nurture)

capture.evidence: 3M+ monthly podcast downloads, bestselling books

portable.evidence: Co-founded MMTCP with Jack Kornfield (2016). RAIN used as clinical tool globally.

profiles.early_revenue_description: Maintained a private clinical psychology practice while leading meditation gatherings.
profiles.ruleBreak: Buddhism and psychotherapy were separate worlds. She merged clinical psychology with Buddhist meditation, then gave it all away for free via podcast before podcasting was mainstream.
profiles.twoWorlds: Clinical psychologist (PhD dissertation on meditation and eating disorders) + Buddhist meditation teacher. Founded IMCW (1998). Co-created MMTCP with Jack Kornfield, graduating 8,000+ teachers in 70+ countries.
profiles.stupidSimplicity: Radical acceptance.
profiles.remarkableResult: Podcast grew to 2.5M+ monthly downloads. RAIN method adopted as a clinical tool worldwide. MMTCP trained 8,000+ meditation teachers in 70+ countries.

profiles.name: Tara Stiles
profiles.bio: A former Ford model who stripped yoga of its spiritual pretense, called it 'Strala,' and partnered with W Hotels and Reebok to make it a lifestyle brand for people who'd never set foot in a yoga studio
profiles.oneLiner: Make your own rules
profiles.blowUpMoment: ~2013. NYT "rebel yoga" profile, Deepak collaboration, W Hotels, multiple books.
profiles.blowUpContext: She was a model in New York who began posting casual yoga videos on YouTube, positioning yoga as accessible fitness rather than spiritual practice.

create.evidence: At peak: Create=strong

capture.evidence: At peak: Capture=starting

portable.evidence: At peak: Portable=starting. Missing: Differentiated methodology. No "Strala teachers" movement.

profiles.ruleBreak: Stripped yoga of its spiritual/Sanskrit/guru trappings and rebranded it as a simple, accessible physical practice. While the yoga establishment insisted on lineage, proper terminology, and spiritual framework, she said 'it's just movement that feels good' — which infuriated yoga purists but opened the practice to millions of people intimidated by the traditional gatekeeping.
profiles.twoWorlds: Fashion modeling (she was a Ford model in NYC) meets yoga instruction. Brought the casual, accessible aesthetic of a model-next-door to a practice that was wrapped in incense and Sanskrit, making yoga feel like something you do in your living room in sweatpants.
profiles.stupidSimplicity: Yoga is just moving your body in a way that feels good — skip the dogma.
profiles.remarkableResult: Strala Yoga trained 1,000+ Guides in 15+ countries. Harvard Business School wrote a case study on her brand. Still actively running international trainings in 2026.

profiles.name: Terry Real
profiles.early_revenue_description: Maintained a full private therapy practice charging per-session fees in Boston.
profiles.ruleBreak: Rejected the therapist-as-neutral-observer model. While most therapists sit back and reflect, he directly confronts clients — especially men — about their grandiosity, entitlement, and relational incompetence. He calls bullshit in session. Also rejected the idea that men's emotional shutdown is just 'how men are' — named it 'covert depression' and said the entire culture is producing relationally disabled men.
profiles.twoWorlds: Grew up with a violent, abusive, depressed father. His own childhood trauma became the foundation for understanding how men hide pain. Combined personal experience of male depression with family systems therapy.
profiles.stupidSimplicity: Most men are depressed and don't know it — and it's destroying their relationships.
profiles.remarkableResult: His book 'I Don't Want to Talk About It' (on male depression) became a classic that reframed how the therapy world thinks about men. Relational Life Therapy (RLT) has trained thousands of therapists. He's become arguably the most prominent voice on men's relational health. His work has experienced a major resurgence in the 2020s through podcasts and social media, reaching a new generation. Continues to sell out workshops and trainings.

profiles.name: Thomas Hübl
profiles.bio: An Austrian-born teacher who developed a framework for healing collective and intergenerational trauma through group mystical practice and relational attunement
profiles.oneLiner: Trauma that is not transformed is transmitted
profiles.blowUpMoment: Built international online following through collective trauma courses and "Attuning to Collective Trauma" work
profiles.blowUpContext: He had been leading online courses and multi-year training programs on collective trauma healing for over a decade, working primarily in German-speaking countries and Israel.

create.evidence: Collective trauma as group process. New category.

capture.evidence: Online courses, retreats, but limited mainstream media

portable.evidence: Training programs exist but still personality-dependent

profiles.ruleBreak: Rejected the individual-only model of trauma healing. While therapy and personal development treated trauma as a personal biographical problem, Hübl argued that much of what individuals carry is actually collective and intergenerational trauma — passed down through family lines and cultural history — and that it must be healed collectively, not just individually.
profiles.twoWorlds: Former medical student and paramedic (9 years) turned contemplative teacher. Now a visiting scholar at Harvard's Wyss Institute. Combined clinical training with mystical practice to address collective trauma.
profiles.stupidSimplicity: Your trauma isn't just yours — it belongs to your lineage, and healing it heals them too.
profiles.remarkableResult: 100K+ course participants. Published in Harvard Health. Visiting scholar at Harvard's Wyss Institute. Built an international framework for healing collective and intergenerational trauma.

profiles.name: Vinn Marti
profiles.blowUpMoment: Codified Soul Motion as a conscious dance practice in early 2000s, now taught globally

create.evidence: Created Soul Motion practice (correction: NOT ecstatic dance founder)

capture.evidence: Kripalu features, YouTube, but no books or mainstream media

portable.evidence: International teacher training, certified teachers globally

profiles.ruleBreak: Rejected the idea that conscious dance must be either a free-form ecstatic release (like 5Rhythms or ecstatic dance) or a structured technique class. While the conscious dance world split into chaos-or-choreography, Marti created Soul Motion as a 'third way' — a practice with enough structure to build skill and mastery, but enough freedom that every dance is a genuine improvisation. He treats movement as a conversation, not a performance or a catharsis.
profiles.twoWorlds: Grew up in the Bronx, served in the military, worked blue-collar factory jobs. Didn't start dance until his mid-20s. Combined working-class grit and discipline with conscious movement practice.
profiles.stupidSimplicity: Keep your soul in motion — dance is not what you do, it is who you are.
profiles.remarkableResult: LOW_CONFIDENCE — Vinn Marti has been teaching movement for over 35 years and Soul Motion is taught by certified teachers across the US, Europe, Latin America, Australia, Japan, and Iceland. However, specific metrics (number of certified teachers, total students, revenue) are not publicly documented in verifiable sources.
